authority: 警視庁 運転免許本部 (Metropolitan Police Department, Driver's Licence Division) — prefectural public safety commission acting under the National Police Agency framework
instrument: 外国免許からの切替え（外免切替）— 道路交通法第97条の２第３項 (confirmation of knowledge and skill) with 道路交通法施行令第34条の４第２項 (waiver of the statutory written and practical tests); list of exempted countries/regions published by the licensing authority
residence_condition: Applicant must have an address in Japan and apply to the prefectural licensing centre for that address (警視庁 states 住所が東京都内の方). Foreign nationals must produce a 住民票 showing 特定事項 (residence status and period) unless they hold MOFA-issued identification. Separately, an origin-side condition: the applicant must have stayed in the issuing country/region for a cumulative three months or more AFTER obtaining the foreign licence, evidenced by passport entry/exit stamps.

entries.note: Japan's 外免切替 is open to holders of any foreign administrative authority's Class 1 licence: 道路交通法施行令第34条の4第2項 waives the statutory 学科試験 and 技能試験 outright, and what remains is the 公安委員会's knowledge and skills confirmation under 道路交通法第97条の2第3項. Origins outside the 29 listed must sit both confirmations, so this row records them as required rather than as a test-free exchange.

notes: Two-layer structure, and it matters: 道路交通法施行令第34条の4第2項 waives the statutory 技能試験 and 学科試験 for ANY holder of a foreign Class 1 licence who stayed 3+ months in the issuing country after obtaining it. What is left is an administrative 知識確認 (knowledge confirmation) and 技能確認 (skills confirmation) under 道路交通法第97条の2第3項. The published 29-country list exempts holders from those two confirmations as well — that list, not the statute, is what makes an exchange test-free.

The 29-country list is the national list; it is published by each prefectural police force. This row cites the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department page (updated 17 August 2026). The NPA's own national page states the framework and the 3-month stay condition but does not reproduce the list: https://www.npa.go.jp/policies/application/license_renewal/have_DL_issed_another_country.html

The NPA national page confirms the 3-month rule verbatim: 「外国等の免許を受けた後、その国等に通算して３か月以上滞在していたことが条件となります」, and that the original foreign licence (not an IDP) must be produced with a Japanese translation prepared by the issuing authority, that country's consulate, JAF, ジップラス or 訪日運転者支援協会.

Sub-national origins: the United States appears only as seven named states for the full exemption (Ohio, Oregon, Colorado, Virginia, Hawaii, Maryland, Washington) and Indiana separately for a skills-only exemption. Australia and Canada, by contrast, ARE listed country-wide by Japan — unlike Germany, Denmark and Switzerland, which treat them provincially. Do not normalise the two patterns to each other.

From 1 October 2025 a 道路交通法施行規則 amendment tightened this route: the knowledge confirmation went from 10 questions with 7 to pass to 50 questions with 45 to pass, illustration questions were dropped, the skills confirmation added tasks such as crossing pedestrian crossings and its marking standards were made stricter, and residence documentation was tightened (住民票 with 特定事項, or MOFA identification plus separate address proof). Source: https://www.keishicho.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/menkyo/oshirase/low.html

grants is recognition_and_exchange because Japan separately RECOGNISES the domestic licences of six jurisdictions for driving without exchange, when accompanied by a prescribed Japanese translation: 「現在、スイス連邦、ドイツ連邦共和国、フランス共和国、ベルギー王国、モナコ公国及び台湾が対象となります」 (NPA page). That is a recognition of the licence itself, not an International Driving Permit instrument, so it is in scope; the IDP/Geneva Convention route is excluded from this layer.

medical_certificate_required is null: the authority publishes eyesight thresholds tested at the counter (0.7 both eyes / 0.3 each for ordinary and motorcycle; 0.8 / 0.5 plus depth perception for semi-medium and above) but says nothing about a medical certificate to be produced. Not recorded is not the same as not required.

Nothing on the authority's page states a deadline for exchanging after taking up residence, so exchange_window_months is null. Separately, a foreign or international licence may be driven on for one year from the date of landing — that is the driving-on-a-foreign-licence rule, not an exchange window.
Whether the foreign licence is surrendered is not stated on this page; the page's only surrender material runs the other way (Japanese licences surrendered abroad).

e-Gov trap confirmed and worked around: laws.e-gov.go.jp's viewer is a single-page app, but https://elaws.e-gov.go.jp/api/1/lawdata/335CO0000000270 returns the real text of 道路交通法施行令, which is where 第34条の4第2項 was read.

instrument: Traffic Police, "Singapore Driving Licence" — Conversion of Foreign Driving Licence to Singapore Driving Licence (administrative criteria and document schedule)
residence_condition: Conversion is compulsory for Singapore citizens, permanent residents, foreigners residing in Singapore for more than 12 months, and foreigners residing under 12 months who are employed as drivers on a Work Permit or S Pass. The origin-side condition is documentary: "Supporting documents to prove 1-year residency in country of issuance of driving licence with a physical residency of at least 6 months in the said country", whose stated purpose is "To determine intention of stay in country is not solely to obtain a driving licence". PRs, pass holders and citizens whose foreign licence was obtained after they got that status must additionally prove a minimum 6-month stay within a 12-month period in the issuing country.
quote_original: Holder of a valid foreign driving licence is allowed to drive for up to three months on Singapore roads upon obtaining the new Singapore citizenship or permanent resident status and will be required to do a conversion of the valid foreign driving licence to a Singapore driving licence, if he/she wishes to continue driving in Singapore.

entries.origin_label_en: Any country or territory issuing a valid full foreign driving licence
entries.classes: Class 3/3A and Class 2B (age 18+); Work Permit and S Pass holders are issued Class 3C on conversion
entries.note: Singapore publishes no list of approved origin countries. The published criteria are only (i) pass the Basic Theory Test in Singapore and (ii) hold a valid foreign driving licence, so the origin state does not gate the exchange — the applicant's own residence history does. No practical test is listed for the ordinary conversion; a practical test is added only for Work Permit/S Pass holders who want Class 3 rather than the Class 3C they are given, or who want to upgrade 3C/3CA to 3/3A.

Extra origin-specific proof: "For Malaysian driving licence holder, a letter from the Road Transport Department Malaysia [Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan Malaysia (JPJ)] showing the breakdown of various class(es) of driving licence and date of issuance together with payment receipt." Malaysia also has its own downloadable checklist.

Extra origin-specific proof: "For Indian driving licence holder, an endorsement letter of validity of driving licence from India Embassy (with payment receipt)." India also has its own downloadable checklist. Note the Traffic Police treat India as a single country here — no state-level split.
Traffic Police publish a separate document checklist for China alongside Malaysia, India and "Other countries".

notes: This is the destination in the region with NO origin list. The gate is the applicant, not the issuing state: pass the Basic Theory Test and hold a valid foreign licence. So every origin carries theory_test_required = true and the layer's usual question — which countries are exchangeable — has the answer "all of them, on the same terms".

The 3-month window in exchange_window_months is the one the quoted sentence states: a new Singapore citizen or permanent resident may drive on the foreign licence for up to three months after acquiring that status and must convert to keep driving. A different clock applies to work-pass drivers: "If you want to drive for work, you will need to obtain a Singapore driving licence within 6 months from the date of issue of your work passes."

Class outcome is stratified by immigration status, not by origin: "All Work Permit & S Pass Holders will be granted a Class 3C licence upon successful conversion of their foreign driving licence", limited to motor cars up to 3,000kg unladen with 7 or fewer passengers, and they "will need to pass a practical driving test, on top of the Basic Theory Test (BTT), if you intend to drive Class 3 vehicles in Singapore". Since 15 September 2025 a Class 3C holder must also pass a road assessment before taking Class 4 lessons, and failing it revokes the 3C.

practical_test_required is false rather than null because the authority states the criteria exhaustively ("The criteria for the conversion of licence are" — BTT plus a valid foreign licence) and introduces the practical test only as an addition "on top of the BTT" for the work-pass class upgrade. It is a stated absence, not an unrecorded field.

Motorcycles are the exception where the origin authority is asked to vouch: for Class 2A and Class 2 the applicant must produce "Proof from the foreign Licensing Authority stating a higher capacity of the motorcycle tested on", signed and endorsed by that authority.

Surrender of the original is not stated on the page, so it is not recorded here. Licences not in English need "Official translation of foreign driving licence by a Singapore registered translation company".

Excluded from this row, deliberately: foreigners residing in Singapore for less than 12 months drive on a foreign licence plus an International Driving Permit, and ASEAN member state licence holders need no IDP at all. That is a visitor-recognition rule, not an exchange, so it is not made a destination fact.
Fee $50, submitted at Traffic Police Headquarters after a FormSG pre-assessment (https://go.gov.sg/foreign-driving-licence-conversion) and an appointment. Page last updated 30 July 2026.
The e-service page https://www.police.gov.sg/E-Services/Book-Appointment-to-Convert-Foreign-Driving-Licence carries the same eligibility criteria in list form and was cross-read.

instrument: Road Traffic (Driving Licences) Regulations (Cap. 374B), Schedule 4 — direct issue of a Hong Kong full driving licence without test
residence_condition: No Hong Kong residence requirement for direct issue. The Transport Department expressly contemplates applicants living outside Hong Kong ("If you reside outside Hong Kong, you may fill in your non-Hong Kong residential address in the application form"), requiring only proof of present address plus a Hong Kong correspondence address. The residence test is on the ORIGIN side and is disjunctive: the licence was issued during a period of residence of not less than 6 months in the issuing place, OR it has been held for not less than 5 years immediately before the application, OR the applicant holds a passport or equivalent travel document of the issuing place.

notes: Direct issue is genuinely test-free: "Applicants meeting all the requirements for direct issue of a full driving licence would be issued with a Hong Kong full driving licence without passing through the 12-month probationary driving period." (https://www.td.gov.hk/en/public_services/licences_and_permits/driving_licences/how_to_apply_for_a_driving_licence/driving_in_hong_kong_for_overseas_driving_licence_/index.html)

Scope limit worth carrying into the map: "The \"direct issue\" mechanism is only applicable to private car, light goods vehicle, motor cycle and motor tricycle." Heavy and public-service classes are not exchangeable by this route.

The foreign licence itself is not surrendered: "Please note that the Transport Department will not keep the original identity documents and driving licences. Such documents will be returned over the counter on the spot." It must, however, be a full licence valid or expired for not more than 3 years, and it must have been obtained by passing the relevant driving test in the issuing place.

medical_certificate_required is false for the ordinary case and that is a recorded limit, not an inference: form TD256 completed by a registered medical practitioner within 4 months of application is required only for "a person aged 70 or above".

Origins NOT in Schedule 4 are not refused outright — they take the temporary-driving-licence route: apply for a driving test within 3 months of arriving to take up residence, drive on a temporary licence valid until the foreign licence expires or 12 months from arrival, whichever is first, and pass the Hong Kong test. That is a test route, not an exchange, so no rows are written for it.

Sub-national handling: Hong Kong lists the United States and Canada country-wide, with no state or province split — the opposite of Japan (seven US states plus Indiana) and of Germany, Denmark and Switzerland. The only sub-national structure in Schedule 4 is inside "China" (Mainland / Taiwan / Macao) and inside the composite United Kingdom item.

From 16 March 2026 direct-issue applications must be booked through the designated online appointment system; no walk-in or on-site queue tickets, and postal or drop-box submission is not accepted. Since 15 September 2025 licences carrying a direct-issue entitlement are numbered with a "DI" prefix and the entitlement is marked with an asterisk.
Appendix C is the Transport Department's own reproduction of Schedule 4 and carries a revision date of 23 September 2025 in the page source.

authority: 交通部公路局（公路監理機關）— Directorate General of Highways, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, through the motor vehicle offices
instrument: 道路交通安全規則 第50條第5項及第6項 (Regulations Governing Road Traffic Safety, Article 50(5)-(6))
residence_condition: The applicant must hold proof of permitted stay or residence of six months or more (經許可停留或居留六個月以上之證明), and may apply from the day after entry (得於入境之翌日起). Nationals of the Republic of China with household registration in Taiwan produce a national identity card or military identity card instead.
quote_original: 持有外國政府、大陸地區、香港或澳門所發有效之正式駕駛執照（證）並取得經許可停留或居留六個月以上之證明（件）者，得於入境之翌日起依平等互惠原則免考換發同等車類之普通駕駛執照。但持有該有效之正式駕駛執照者而具有中華民國國籍時，得免考換發同等車類之普通駕駛執照。
quote_translation: A person holding a valid formal driving licence (or permit) issued by a foreign government, the mainland area, Hong Kong or Macao who has obtained proof of permitted stay or residence of six months or more may, from the day after entry, in accordance with the principle of equality and reciprocity, exchange it without examination for an ordinary driving licence of the same class of vehicle. However, where the holder of such a valid formal driving licence has Republic of China nationality, the exchange without examination for an ordinary driving licence of the same class of vehicle is available [without that condition].

entries.origin_label_en: Any foreign government whose licences Taiwan treats as reciprocal
entries.classes: 普通駕駛執照 of the same vehicle class as the foreign licence (ordinary, non-professional)
entries.note: The regulation grants exchange 免考 (without examination) to holders of a valid formal licence issued by a foreign government, but only 依平等互惠原則 — on the principle of equal reciprocity. The regulation itself does not name the reciprocal states; the operative list is maintained administratively by 公路局. That list could not be retrieved from an official host during this run (see notes), so no per-country rows are asserted.

notes: The exchange is 免考 — without examination — so theory and practical are both false, but the whole grant is conditioned on 平等互惠原則 (equality and reciprocity). Which foreign governments satisfy that is not in the regulation; it is an administrative list published by 公路局. I could not retrieve that list from an official host: www.thb.gov.tw returns a 200 that is an Incapsula bot-challenge shell (959 bytes, no content), www.mvdis.gov.tw (監理服務網) times out at TCP level from this network, tpcmv.thb.gov.tw returns a 212-byte stub, and data.gov.tw's dataset search endpoint 404s. Treat the per-country reciprocity list as OPEN.

A genuine ROC-nationality carve-out sits in the same paragraph: a holder of the foreign licence who has Republic of China nationality gets the examination-free exchange without the reciprocity qualifier attaching in the same way. Worth flagging for anyone reading this layer alongside the citizenship layer.
medical_certificate_required is true and stated: 「汽車駕駛人辦理前項換發手續時，應先經體格檢查合格」 — the applicant must first pass a physical examination before the exchange formalities.

Authentication burden is origin-specific and set out in the same article: mainland permits must be verified by an Executive Yuan institution; Hong Kong and Macao licences by an Executive Yuan institution in those places; all other foreign licences by an ROC embassy, representative office or foreign mission in Taiwan authorised for document certification; and a licence in a language other than English needs a Chinese translation verified the same way.

Article 55 of the same regulation, which is what a search for Taiwan driving-licence exchange surfaces first, is the INTERNATIONAL DRIVING PERMIT article (issue and endorsement of IDPs, 30-day visa-free short stay for reciprocal-country IDP holders). It is excluded from this layer.
Class scope: the exchange produces a 普通駕駛執照 (ordinary licence) of the same vehicle class. Professional (職業) licences are not obtained by this route.

authority: Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan Malaysia (JPJ) — Road Transport Department, Bahagian Pelesenan Pemandu
notes: JPJ's own site confirms the function EXISTS — the Driver Licensing Division's listed functions include 「Mengendalikan urusan pertukaran lesen memandu asing dan rayuan」 (handling foreign driving licence exchange matters and appeals) — but publishes no conditions, no country list and no test/waiver detail anywhere I could reach.

What I tried: www.jpj.gov.my home and the Bahagian Pelesenan Pemandu page (both 200, parsed in full, no exchange content beyond the functions list); the JPJ driving-licence FAQ at /pusat-media-3/soalan-lazim/soalan-lazim-lesen-memandu/ (200, 494KB, contains no occurrence of "asing"); malaysia.gov.my site search for "pertukaran lesen memandu asing" (200 but returned no parseable result links). Web search was unavailable for this run (session search budget exhausted), and mojeek/duckduckgo HTML endpoints returned bot challenges, so I could not locate the instrument number to cite.

Next step for whoever picks this up: the governing rules are almost certainly the Motor Vehicles (Driving Licence) Rules made under the Road Transport Act 1987 (Akta 333). JPJ links its own copy of Akta 333 at https://www.jpj.gov.my/akta-333/ — start there, then look for the JPJ circular or the Pekeliling that names the recognised countries.
No absence is asserted here. This row records that the arrangement exists and that its terms were not verifiable, not that Malaysia refuses exchange.

authority: กรมการขนส่งทางบก (Department of Land Transport, Ministry of Transport)
notes: The Department of Land Transport is unreachable from this network: https://www.dlt.go.th/ resets the connection at TCP level (curl 35, "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer"), and http://www.dlt.go.th/, https://dlt.go.th/ and https://www.dlt.go.th/th/public-news/ all return 000 with zero bytes. WebFetch against the same host failed with ECONNRESET and a closed socket. Add dlt.go.th to the blocked-hosts list alongside the other unreachable publishers.
No secondary route was acceptable: everything reachable about Thai licence conversion is relocation agencies and expat forums, which this layer does not use.

Next step: the primary instrument is under พระราชบัญญัติรถยนต์ พ.ศ. 2522 (Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522) and its ministerial regulations; the Royal Gazette (ratchakitcha.soc.go.th) is the citable publisher if DLT stays unreachable. Do not confuse the exchange route with Thailand's recognition of International Driving Permits under the 1949 Geneva Convention, which is out of scope here.

authority: Land Transportation Office (LTO), Department of Transportation
notes: lto.gov.ph sits behind a Cloudflare interstitial: https://lto.gov.ph/ and https://www.lto.gov.ph/ both return HTTP 403 with a "Just a moment..." The only reachable LTO host is https://portal.lto.gov.ph/ (LTMS Online Portal, 200), which is an Oracle APEX login application with no public policy text.

What is missing is the LTO memorandum circular that governs conversion of a foreign licence for a foreign national with an appropriate visa, and whether the written and practical examinations are waived. Without the circular text I will not guess at the test fields.

Next step: try the Official Gazette (officialgazette.gov.ph) or the Department of Transportation for the LTO memorandum circular, or retry lto.gov.ph from a network that clears the Cloudflare challenge.
